subject.title: feat: AI safety event taxonomy — plugin emission API and manifest policy

question: Should OpenClaw adopt plugin-emitted AI-safety events, and if so must the permanent contract be a host-created capability with authoritative identity and complete runtime validation?
rationale: This introduces a new public plugin API and operator-facing safety signal whose authority, taxonomy stability, and trust semantics are product and security policy choices rather than mechanical implementation details.

options.title: Adopt a host-owned capability
options.body: Approve the feature direction only after redesigning the API as a bound host-created emitter with normalized permissions, authoritative provenance, full validation, documentation, and installed-plugin proof.

options.title: Keep safety events core-owned
options.body: Reject external plugin emission and limit the taxonomy to trusted core or bundled-plugin producers until a narrower extension contract is justified.

options.title: Pause the taxonomy series
options.body: Close or pause the related PR series if operator-facing AI-safety telemetry is not a current product priority.

recommendation.title: Adopt a host-owned capability
recommendation.body: Approve the feature direction only after redesigning the API as a bound host-created emitter with normalized permissions, authoritative provenance, full validation, documentation, and installed-plugin proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent plugin context and runtime-surface history makes this the strongest available owner for the public capability and trust-boundary decision.
